packs.title: Hills, Art and Ocean
packs.promise: Explore Los Angeles through Hollywood landmarks, art, ancient landscapes and the Pacific.

q.s: Make a new composition from lettering and landscape.
st: Use a permitted park viewpoint and leave residential entrances clear.
Notice the relationship between the hillside and distant sign.
Draw or describe an original landscape frame, changing the arrangement of the hillside and lettering rather than tracing the sign.

q.s: Connect a sidewalk tribute to the work it recognizes.
st: Choose one nearby honoree using the official star directory.
Read its official profile and record one credited contribution.
Write what you would like to learn or watch next.

q.s: Notice how a theme park uses design to suggest a story.
st: Choose open guest areas included in your admission.
Find a detail suggesting scale, one suggesting a setting and one directing attention.
Describe which makes the strongest impression.

packs.title: City in the Frame
packs.promise: Find ten small adventures inside Downtown’s changing scenes.

q.s: Collect a market palette without buying a thing.
st: Enter only during posted public hours and choose a spot outside ordering lines.
Collect five details across any senses that work for you: a color, a shape, a texture, an aroma, or a sound. You may use one sense for all five.
Choose the detail that feels most unlike the others and note what makes it stand out.
Save the palette in a field note or one people-free photograph with a short caption.

q.s: Give the concert hall an opening scene of your own.
st: Find a legal resting spot on the public sidewalk with part of the concert hall in view.
Compose a wide opening frame, a close detail, and a final frame using its curved exterior and the street around it.
Give each imagined frame one action verb. Your scene can be described entirely in words.
Save three short frame descriptions or a people-free photograph with your three-frame plan.

q.s: Watch a hill turn into a tiny journey.
st: Start from either publicly accessible station area and check the posted service and fare information.
Choose one normal passenger ride if the fare and boarding work for you, or observe the railway from outside the paid area.
Notice a detail that changes with height and a detail that stays in place. If the cars are stopped, compare the lower and upper portions visible from your position.
Save the two details with a sentence about how the hill changes your view.
